description:
Hello from Uruguay! 🇺🇾🚀

We are Astro Girls, a team of students from Santa Elena School in Uruguay, excited to participate in the NASA Space Apps Challenge! 🌎✨
summary: Fire in Space is a web application created to explain how fire behaves without gravity, developed for the Flame in Free Fall challenge by Francesca, Pilar, Victoria, Guillermina and Delfina, students from Uruguay. We started by writing a prompt describing our idea to an AI, Claude, and used it to build an app that we published online. On Earth, hot gases rise and create convection currents that feed the flame with fresh oxygen, giving it its long, upward shape. In space, without gravity, flames become spherical, burn cooler and appear blue, because oxygen reaches them more evenly from all sides. Understanding these differences is essential for keeping astronauts safe, and our app helps students and the public discover this surprising science in a simple and visual way.
details:
What it does and how it works. The app explains the science of fire in microgravity and compares a candle flame on Earth with a flame in space.

The science behind it. On Earth, a flame is long and yellow because hot gases rise and pull fresh oxygen from below. In microgravity there is no convection, so the flame becomes round, burns at a lower temperature and glows blue. NASA studies this in space laboratories to understand combustion and improve fire safety on missions.

Benefits and intended impact. The app makes a complex topic easy to understand for anyone with a phone or computer, and it is available online for free.

Tools used. Claude (an AI assistant) to help design and program the app, Netlify to publish it online, and Canva for the presentation.

Creativity. We learned how to turn an idea into a working website by explaining it clearly to an AI, which is exactly how the Flame in Free Fall challenge invites teams to use AI to study fire.

Factors we considered. How to explain the differences between fire on Earth and in space clearly, and how to make the information visual and accessible.
